children: dropped 7.17% to $320.79 at the 4:00 p.m. ET close on November 17 as the software selloff collided with worries that AI assistants could take over personal finance tasks. Startup Fortune linked the pressure to Anthropic's Personal Finance in Claude beta, which lets users connect bank accounts and query two years of transactions.

Intuit reports fiscal first-quarter results on November 19 after the close. Its own guidance calls for revenue of $4.294 billion to $4.313 billion, up 11%, and non-GAAP EPS of $2.44 to $2.48. For fiscal 2027, the company expects revenue growth of only 9% to 10% after 14% in fiscal 2026, alongside non-GAAP EPS of $22.88 to $23.12, with TurboTax revenue having grown just 7% last year.

The midpoint EPS guide puts the shares at about 13.9 times forward earnings, a multiple that already assumes slower growth. GuruFocus gives Intuit a GF Score of 81/100, combining elite profitability with badly broken momentum. Its GF Value of $840.52 puts the close about 62% below the model, a significantly undervalued reading that likely reflects years of premium multiples the market no longer grants. Thursday's report is the immediate test: a beat with steady fiscal 2027 guidance could ease disruption fears, while any cut would validate them.

title: Intuit Stocks Fall 7.17% Two Days Before Earnings as AI Finance Tools Loom
